Cardiff Council in Wales, United Kingdom has approved plans allowing the highly anticipated heavyweight boxing clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua to run into the early hours of the morning, with alcohol sales permitted until 3am. The approval was granted by the council’s Licensing Sub Committee ahead of the December 11 fight at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. As reported by the BBC, under the arrangement, hospitality boxes at the stadium will be allowed to serve alcohol until 3am, while the venue is expected to close at 3:30am to accommodate prime-time television coverage in the United States. The fight’s ring walk is scheduled for 1am on December 12, with the opening bell expected at approximately 1:30am, according to stadium director Mark Williams. Williams told councillors that the extended hours were necessary to accommodate the event’s schedule and confirmed that tickets were still available. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. To maintain security and public order, 130 police officers will be deployed, alongside twice the number of stewards normally provided for a regular sporting event. Councillors were also informed that 450 of the 1,600 stewards would be assigned specifically to spectators seated on the stadium’s pitch area. ‘They are scared’, Ajagba frustrated by lack of opponents Joshua talks retirement ahead Fury fight Fury opens up on mental health struggles after 2015 Klitschko victory South Wales Police Chief Inspector Huw Thomas described the event as a major security operation, noting that the length of the programme meant officers were treating it as a “three-day event”. Some residents had raised objections over concerns about noise, antisocial behaviour and public safety, although none attended the licensing meeting. However, the council was assured that measures had been put in place to address the concerns, including additional early-morning train services and restrictions on external public address systems. The meeting also heard that breathalysers would be used at stadium entrances for spectators who appeared intoxicated. Chair of the Licensing Sub Committee, Grace Ferguson-Thorne, said the panel was reassured by the security and crowd-management arrangements, including the planned stewarding levels and closure of the stadium roof. The approval marks another occasion when the Principality Stadium will host a major boxing event extending into the early hours. In 2007, Joe Calzaghe’s victory over Mikkel Kessler began at approximately 2am to accommodate television audiences in the United States. The 2018 heavyweight contest between Anthony Joshua and Joseph Parker also attracted more than 78,000 spectators, setting an attendance record for an event at the stadium.
